item: grep PATTERN FILE...: the first operand is the pattern, the rest are files
-e PATTERNS: repeated, and newline separated patterns in one argument
-f FILE: patterns from a file (an empty file has no pattern: nothing matches)
options may follow the operands; `--` ends them
long options, their unambiguous abbreviations, --option=value and --option value
-NUM is -C NUM; the digits of one argument make one number
an invalid option, a missing argument or a missing pattern: usage message, status 2
invalid values: context length, max count, -d, -D, -X, --binary-files, conflicting matchers
standard input: no file operand, `-`, and --label
egrep and fgrep are grep -E and grep -F
exit status: 0 for a selected line, 1 for none, 2 for an error
-s hides the messages about files, the status is still 2
obsolete options -y (as -i) and -u (a warning)
notes: -u is an invalid option from grep 3.12 on

item: basic regular expressions: literals, `.`, `*`, `^` and `$`
basic regular expressions, GNU operators: \+ \? \| \( \) and back-references
intervals: \{m\} \{m,\} \{,n\} \{m,n\} (ERE: {m,n})
bracket expressions: sets, ranges, negation, a first ], classes, equivalence classes
extended regular expressions: + ? | ( ) { } and back-references
ERE: an operator at the start of an expression is skipped with a warning
ERE: an invalid interval and an unmatched ) are characters; BRE: a leading \{ is a character
BRE: a leading * is a character; an operator after an anchor
a backslash before an ordinary character: no sed escapes (\n \t), the character itself
-F: fixed strings, several, with characters that are special in regular expressions
-i and --no-ignore-case
-w: the match is a whole word; a shorter match at the same place is tried
-x: the match is the whole line; -x with -w
-v selects the lines that do not match
several patterns: the leftmost, then the longest match for -o and --color
the empty pattern matches every line; -v with it selects none
patterns that do not compile: the message and status 2
-z: ^ and $ and . with records that end in NUL
UTF-8: characters, classes, -i, -w, -o
patterns with a back-reference: the lines and the matches
-n: line numbers
-b: byte offsets (of the line, of the match with -o)
-H and -h: file names in front of lines (several files, -r)
-c: counts, with names for several files
-l: names of the files with a selected line
-L: names of the files with none
-q: no output, exit at the first selected line
-m NUM: stop after NUM selected lines
-o: only the matches, one per line; empty matches are not printed
-o with -b, -n, -v, -i, -c
-T: the numbers have a width and a tab follows the prefix
-Z: a NUL after the file name
a last line without a newline gets one; CRLF is kept; --line-buffered
-q over -l and -L over -c; -c with -v; -m 0
option combinations of the output
-A, -B, -C: lines of context, `-` after the file name and numbers
the group separator `--`, --group-separator and --no-group-separator
context with -n, -b, -H and with several files
-m with context: the trailing context after the last selected line
-v with context
-o, -c and -l with context
context near the start and the end, overlapping groups
a directory operand: `Is a directory`, -d read, skip and recurse
-r and -R: names, no operand means `.` without a leading ./, symlinks
--include, --exclude and --exclude-from: the last matching pattern decides
--exclude-dir
-D read and skip

a regular file on standard input is left after the last selected line with -m
large files and long lines: line numbers, offsets and context across the pieces read

-a and --binary-files=text
-I and --binary-files=without-match
binary files with -c, -l, -L, -q, -o, -v, -m, context
